question: author, 2026-11-08: can any material be used better than cement and steel?

rc_conventional.label: Reinforced concrete frame, fired brick or block infill (today's standard)
rc_conventional.basis: materials: Heeren & Fishman 2019 medians (VERIFIED); CO2 400 and labour 48: v70 central values

rc_lc3.label: Same building with LC3 limestone calcined clay cement
rc_lc3.basis: LC3 cuts cement CO2 by up to 40% using abundant low-grade clays in existing plants (lc3.ch, VERIFIED); 0.6 kg CO2 per kg of ordinary cement (REPORTED); only the cement share of the building's CO2 changes

timber_frame.label: Light timber frame, 1-3 storeys
timber_frame.where: temperate and boreal forest regions; tropical where forests are managed
timber_frame.basis: wood 0.16-0.22 m3/m2 for timber-frame homes incl. insulation and cladding (REPORTED); cement for foundations and steel for fasteners ASSUMPTION; CO2 150 = v70 low-carbon central; labour between the Finnish precast benchmark (13) and site-built (48), ASSUMPTION

clt_midrise.label: Cross-laminated timber, 4-8 storeys
clt_midrise.where: dense cities in or near forest regions
clt_midrise.basis: CLT use factors 0.149-0.457 m3 per m2 of footprint per storey, most above 0.305 (Dolan et al. 2019 citing Crespell & Gagnon 2010, VERIFIED); cement for foundations and cores, steel connectors, CO2 and labour ASSUMPTION

bamboo_frame.label: Engineered bamboo or bahareque frame, 1-3 storeys
bamboo_frame.where: humid tropics (South and South-East Asia, Central Africa, Latin America)
bamboo_frame.basis: bamboo buildings about 30 kg CO2e/m2 (Escamilla 2018, cited in v70) and a Colombian bamboo house about 107 (unverified): 60 is judgement; bamboo mass per m2 (30-60 kg) ASSUMPTION, the inventory paper could not be read (publisher refuses automated access); cement for foundations and render ASSUMPTION; needs treatment against borers and fungi

earth_vault.label: Compressed or raw earth walls with earth vault roofs, 1-2 storeys
earth_vault.where: dry and semi-arid regions (Sahel, Horn of Africa, South Asia's dry zones, Middle East, Andes)
earth_vault.basis: Nubian Vault programme: 8,500+ buildings, 4,900+ trained masons, 7 Sahel countries, 'based exclusively on local raw earth' (lavoutenubienne.org, VERIFIED); cement 0-15 kg for optional stabilised blocks, earth mass, CO2 and labour (PMAY-G upper value 64 h/m2) ASSUMPTION; limited to low rise and to climates with little driving rain

cement_mt_per_yr.basis: USGS MCS 2025/2026, 3.8-4.1 bn t (PDF refuses automated fetch)

industrial_roundwood_mm3_per_yr.basis: FAO forest products statistics, 2020 table: roundwood 3,912, wood fuel 1,928, industrial roundwood 1,984 million m3

forest_area_bn_ha.basis: FAO FRA 2020 key findings: 4.06 billion ha, nearly a third of land

plantation_forest_mha.basis: FAO FRA 2020: plantation forests about 131 million ha, 3% of forest area

bamboo_area_mha.basis: FAO FRA 2020 bamboo area about 35 million ha; not read in source this session

bamboo_yield_t_ha_yr.basis: Dendrocalamus giganteus 20-30 t/ha/yr dry (commercial nursery claim); 10 as a conservative value

plantation_wood_yield_m3_ha_yr.basis: managed temperate forests about 3-5 m3/ha/yr, tropical plantations 10-20

reading: no single material replaces cement and steel for 7 billion m2 a year: all-timber would take about two-thirds of the world's industrial roundwood, and all-bamboo half to all of today's bamboo area at reported yields, in a climate that holds 44-81% of the people in need. A regional mix does the job: bamboo in the humid tropics, earth with vault roofs in dry regions, timber where forests are managed, cross-laminated timber in dense cities, and LC3 cement where concrete is still needed. It cuts cement to about 40% of the conventional programme, steel to 40%, and embodied CO2 by about 60%, with about the same hours of work, more of them local and low-skill. Its weak point is wood: about a third of today's industrial roundwood, like the conventional programme itself. LC3 alone saves only about 8% of a building's embodied CO2, because cement is a fifth of it: the frame, floors and roof are where the carbon is.
limits: bamboo mass per m2 and bamboo area are not verified; yields are commercial claims
earth and bamboo systems are limited to 1-3 storeys and to their climates; durability depends on treatment, detailing and maintenance (driving rain, termites, earthquakes)
labour per m2 for timber, bamboo and earth systems are assumptions; earth is deliberately labour-intensive
the mix shares are a design proposal, not an optimisation; the latitude test uses capitals only
the conventional system's wood (41.6 kg/m2) is the median of a Europe-heavy sample with many timber homes and probably overstates wood in concrete-frame homes of the regions in need
wood: harvesting 0.6-0.8 bn m3 a year for housing competes with paper, fuel and furniture; plantation expansion has land and biodiversity costs not modelled
